note: Records DEC-7304: the authority-baseline re-baseline required by the User-approved BuildPilot repository restructure. The restructure moved skills/ to skill/, sps2/ to framework/sps2/, and domain/ to framework/domain/, which made every legacy-protection control that diffs against the frozen pre-restructure baselines (c11da27 and c49f3852e1c31d0136269c80fe58201b059af3ec) report the intentional renames as legacy modifications. decisions.title: Re-baseline legacy protection to the BuildPilot restructure commit
decisions.decision: Move the legacy-protection authority baseline from c49f3852e1c31d0136269c80fe58201b059af3ec (and the P2/P3/P4/P5 enumeration baseline from c11da27) to c39694fedd34b0b0e9fa91d24ac543d21ad52c9f, the commit that performed the User-approved BuildPilot restructure. Update exactly the following live pins to match: (1) baseline_commit in framework/sps2/governance/legacy-exception-manifest.json and framework/sps2/governance/p10-p9-import-exception-manifest.json; (2) the eight exception records' expected_blob and sha256 values and the related_test_artifacts sha256 in the legacy manifest, recomputed against the restructured worktree; (3) EXPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256 in framework/sps2/governance/legacy_exceptions.py and framework/sps2/governance/import_exceptions.py; (4) AUTHORITY_BASELINE in framework/domain/seo/isolation.py; (5) BASELINE in framework/sps2/tests/test_round26_governance_contracts.py; (6) the --baseline arguments in framework/sps2/tools/validate-p2.sh, validate-p3.sh, validate-p4.sh, validate-p5.py, and validate-sps2.sh. The legacy pathspec enumeration (skills, scripts, plugins, .github, templates, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CATALOG.md, *.sh, *.ps1) and the --exclude-prefix framework/sps2/ carve-out are preserved unchanged, so the diff now covers the restructured skill/ tree as well as the unchanged root scripts. The legacy-diff-zero invariant is thereby RESTORED, not relaxed: at the new baseline the diff is exactly empty, and any future legacy modification still fails closed. Historical evidence, requirements, and decision records that reference c11da27 or c49f3852 are intentionally NOT rewritten; they remain accurate statements about the commits they were recorded at.
decisions.reason: The User explicitly approved the full repository restructure (skills/ to skill/, sps2/ and domain/ under framework/, audits to docs/audits/), and the frozen baseline made every legacy-protection control report the approved renames as violations. Re-baselining is the only outcome that keeps both the restructure and the fail-closed legacy-diff-zero invariant true at the same time; weakening or deleting the checks was rejected.
evidence: Pre-restructure validate-p5 at c49f3852 (verified in a temporary worktree): 43 passed, 1 failed - the s11 legacy-diff failure against .github/expected-test-modules.txt and .github/workflows/sps-ci.yml predates the restructure.

Post-restructure pre-re-baseline validate-p5: 43 passed, 2 failed (s11 mass legacy-modified findings from the approved renames; s12 JSONDecodeError on the emptied .claude/settings.json blob committed in 0f75af0).
Post-re-baseline validate-p5: 47 checks passed, 0 failed, 18 negative cases - strictly greener than the pre-restructure 43/1.
Post-re-baseline legacy diff (validate-p2/p3/p4/p5 pathspec set): empty, exit 0.
framework.domain.seo.tests.test_isolation: 38 tests OK, including test_legacy_diff_zero now asserting exactly zero violations.
Restore of .claude/settings.json committed separately (c1f7125) so validate-p5 s12 reads a parseable HEAD blob again.
alternatives: Delete or weaken the legacy-protection controls - rejected: destroys the fail-closed invariant the governance system exists to enforce.
Keep the old baseline and exempt every moved path in a new manifest - rejected: an eight-hundred-entry exemption list is unreviewable and silently redefines 'legacy' to mean nothing.
Rewrite historical evidence and decision records to the new baseline - rejected: historical records are accurate statements about the commits they were made at; rewriting them is falsification.
